blurb: a cyclone carries Dorothy to the Land of Oz, and a yellow brick road leads to the Emerald City.
source: Text: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), from the Standard Ebooks edition. Public domain.

streets.name: The Cyclone
streets.blurb: A great cyclone lifts Dorothy’s little grey house right off the Kansas prairie.
streets.how: Race through the storm! Jump the flying fences and dodge the rolling logs until the house comes down gently in Oz.

streets.name: The Scarecrow
streets.blurb: Dorothy sets off along the yellow brick road and meets a Scarecrow on a pole.
streets.how: Find six yellow bricks to start the road, then help the Scarecrow down from his pole.

finale.say: Thank you! It is very tiresome being stuck up on a pole. Do you think, if I go to the Emerald City with you, that Oz would give me some brains?

streets.name: The Tin Woodman
streets.blurb: In the forest stands a man made entirely of tin, rusted solid with his axe raised.
streets.how: Pick up the oil drops and oil the Tin Woodman’s joints in the right order: neck first, then arms, then legs.

params.done: He can move again! “Do you suppose Oz could give me a heart?”

streets.name: The Cowardly Lion
streets.blurb: A great Lion joins them — and on the road they meet a deep ditch and the fierce Kalidahs.
streets.how: Run! Jump the ditches and keep ahead of the Kalidah.

streets.name: The Deadly Poppy Field
streets.blurb: A great meadow of scarlet poppies — and their scent makes everyone sleepy.
streets.how: Get through the poppy field before you fall asleep. The field mice are scattered along the way — collect them, they’ll help!

params.objective: Get through before you fall asleep!

streets.name: The Emerald City
streets.blurb: Everything is green in the Emerald City — and the great Oz looks different to everyone who meets him.
streets.how: Look at the clues in the Throne Room, then work out what is going on.

params.objective: Work out the secret of the Great Oz

clues.label: The green spectacles
clues.text: Everyone in the city must wear green spectacles, locked on with a little key.

clues.label: What the others saw
clues.text: Dorothy saw a great Head. The Scarecrow saw a lovely Lady. The Tin Woodman saw a terrible Beast. The Lion saw a Ball of Fire.

clues.label: The throne
clues.text: The same emerald throne every time. Only the shape on it changes.

solve.label: The secret
solve.prompt: Why does Oz look different to each of them?
options: He is putting on different disguises
He really can change into anything
The green spectacles change what you see
solve.hint: If it is always the same throne, who might be behind it?

streets.name: The Wicked Witch of the West
streets.blurb: The Wicked Witch of the West sends her wolves, crows and bees after the travellers.
streets.how: Dodge the wolves, crows and bees for 30 seconds!

params.objective: Dodge the wolves, crows and bees!
params.done: They’ve all run off! Now for the Witch’s castle.

streets.name: The Winged Monkeys
streets.blurb: In the Witch’s cupboard Dorothy finds a Golden Cap with a charm — and the Winged Monkeys must obey whoever wears it.
streets.how: Climb the tall tree where the Winged Monkeys tossed the Scarecrow’s clothes, up to the Golden Cap.

item.name: A bit of the Scarecrow’s stuffing

streets.name: The Wizard Revealed
streets.blurb: The friends come back to claim their reward — and Toto knocks over a screen in the corner.
streets.how: Look round the Throne Room, then say who the Great Oz really is.

params.objective: Find out who the Great Oz really is

clues.label: The screen
clues.text: Toto jumped back from the Lion’s roar and tipped over the screen in the corner.

clues.label: The Head
clues.text: The great Head is made of many thicknesses of paper, with a carefully painted face. It hangs from the ceiling on a wire.

clues.label: The bran
clues.text: A measure of bran mixed with pins and needles — “bran-new brains” for the Scarecrow.

solve.label: Behind the screen
solve.prompt: Who is the Great and Terrible Oz?
options: A little old man from Omaha — a humbug
solve.hint: What was standing where the screen had been?

streets.name: The Balloon
streets.blurb: Oz is leaving in a great silk balloon — and Dorothy must reach the basket in time.
streets.how: Climb up to the balloon basket before it floats away!

streets.name: The Journey South
streets.blurb: On the way to Glinda: the fighting trees, the dainty China Country and the Hammer-Heads.
streets.how: Make your way south. Dodge the swinging branches, step carefully through the China Country and jump the gaps.

skyRun.name: Over the Poppy Fields
skyRun.blurb: a flight with the Winged Monkeys, high over the scarlet poppy fields.
skyRun.how: Hop from cloud to cloud above the poppies. Some clouds drift — time your jumps.

npcs.name: the Scarecrow
npcs.idle: I don’t mind my legs and arms being stuffed, because I cannot get hurt.
npcs.thanks: Plump and comfortable again — thank you!

steps.text: Talk to the Scarecrow outside the Land of Oz.
steps.say: The Winged Monkeys pulled out all my straw and threw it about! Could you find six bundles to stuff me again?

steps.text: Find six bundles of straw around the district.
Bring the straw back to the Scarecrow.
steps.say: Ah! I feel quite myself again.

vault.name: Glinda’s Palace
vault.blurb: an escape room about the whole journey: what did each friend already have all along?
vault.intro: Glinda the Good sits on her throne of rubies. Before Dorothy can go home, three locks must open — and the answers have been with you the whole way.

stations.label: The four gifts
stations.text: Each friend asked the Wizard for something they thought they lacked. Match each friend to what they had shown all along the road.
stations.lesson: The Scarecrow had good ideas, the Woodman was kind, the Lion was brave — long before the Wizard gave them anything.

pairs: Brains — he thought of the plans
A heart — he was kind to every creature
Courage — he leapt the ditch and faced danger
The Silver Shoes that could take her home
solve.hint: Think about what each friend did on the road, not what they asked for.

stations.label: The Silver Shoes
stations.text: The Silver Shoes, taken from the Witch of the East on Dorothy’s very first day in Oz.
stations.lesson: Dorothy could have gone home on her very first day — if she had known.

solve.prompt: How do the Silver Shoes work?
options: Knock the heels together three times and say where you want to go
Throw them up into the air
solve.hint: Glinda tells Dorothy exactly what to do.

vault.openText: Click, click, click — the door opens onto the road home.
vault.outro: Dorothy knocks her heels together three times, and she is home with Aunt Em. The Oz books that come next are still under the fog.
